public.scenario: Synthetic contrastive retry semantics, set B
public.task: For each mutating operation, decide whether a stable exact request key has an explicit, durable duplicate-suppression guarantee, or only supports tracing or an unsupported best-effort claim. Every operation is synthetic.

operations.description: Enrollment uses the same client nonce in each request. The server retains a stable nonce-to-device mapping and guarantees identical-nonce retries only read that mapping; a second registration is not produced.

Enrollment uses the same client nonce in each request. The server retains a temporary nonce log but gives no guarantee that identical-nonce retries only read that log; a second registration may be produced.
Each message has a message-reference value. Duplicates with the same reference are acknowledged using a new delivery receipt; the message is sent and billed a second time.
Each message has a message-reference value. Duplicates with the same reference are acknowledged using the first delivery receipt, without sending or billing the message a second time.
Issues a voucher with stable issuance_id. A retransmission of issuance_id after an ambiguous acknowledgment retrieves the original voucher; server-side uniqueness prevents duplicate voucher creation.

Issues a voucher with stable issuance_id. A retransmission of issuance_id after an ambiguous acknowledgment carries that ID for audit only; server-side uniqueness does not prevent duplicate voucher creation.
Read-only status inspection, which may lag after a write. Does not itself create an external business effect.
